mhl.name: Aaron Friedman Marine Hydrodynamics Laboratory
mhl.summary: Century-old NAME experimental facility for marine and hydrodynamic testing. Facilities include a towing tank and wind-wave tank. Work covers calm-water resistance, seakeeping, propeller tests, and cutting-edge instrumentation / data acquisition for marine experiments.

bernitsas-michael.summary: Michael Bernitsas directs the Marine Renewable Energy Laboratory and pioneered VIVACE (Vortex Induced Vibrations for Aquatic Clean Energy), converting underwater vortex-induced cylinder oscillations into mechanical/electrical power. His group bridges offshore structural hydrodynamics with marine renewable energy, including river and ocean testing pathways and MHL towing-tank experiments.

ceccio-steven-l.summary: Steven Ceccio works on fluid mechanics of multiphase and high-Reynolds-number flows, including cavitation, propulsors/turbomachinery, friction drag reduction, and development of flow diagnostics. His experimental diagnostics focus is one of the strongest NAME bridges to plasma/optical instrumentation and DAQ-heavy lab work.

collette-matthew-d.summary: Matthew Collette leads the Marine Structures Design Lab, which develops next-generation platform reliability, design science, and lifecycle support tools for the marine industry. The lab combines machine learning, digital twins, and probabilistic methods with an exclusive marine-domain focus, and he is also linked to the Great Lakes Maritime and BRIDGE initiatives.

dong-pingsha.summary: Pingsha Dong focuses on advanced design and analysis of engineering structures, especially welded structures, and novel computational modeling for manufacturing processes. His methods have been adopted into ASME/API codes for fatigue and fitness-for-service evaluation of welded systems used across marine and industrial structures.

dowling-david-r.summary: David Dowling (NAME Chair) researches acoustics and fluid mechanics using experimental, theoretical, and computational techniques. Projects often collaborate with Ceccio and others on fluid-dynamic and acoustic wave problems relevant to marine and offshore design performance, with historical ONR/DARPA support.

ganesh-harish.summary: Harish Ganesh is an Associate Research Scientist whose research centers on fluid dynamics with emphasis on hydrodynamic cavitation and experimental methods. This is a hands-on experimental hydrodynamics role tightly adjacent to instrumentation, optical diagnostics, and multiphase test operations.

ghaffari-maani.summary: Maani Ghaffari directs CURLY, developing algorithms for robot autonomy in unstructured, dynamic, and uncertain environments. Expertise spans geometric state estimation, control, motion planning, and mapping for mobile robots, including marine/robotics joint appointments — a strong autonomy and sensing bridge.

hofmann-heath.summary: Heath Hofmann (EECS, joint NAME) works on power electronics and electromechanical systems, including energy harvesting, flywheel storage, and design/control of electric machines. Relevant to marine electric propulsion and energy systems that need controls and electromechanical hardware support.

mahesh-krishnan.summary: Krishnan Mahesh leads computational research on complex, multi-physics turbulent flows relevant to naval and marine systems. His Computational Fluids Laboratory develops simulation methods for high-fidelity turbulence and multi-physics problems rather than wet-lab diagnostics, but remains a core NAME hydrodynamics contact.

maki-kevin-j.summary: Kevin Maki is Director of the Aaron Friedman Marine Hydrodynamics Laboratory and works in marine computational mechanics for performance evaluation of marine vehicles. He couples full ship finite-element models with nonlinear fluid models (breaking waves, turbulence) for extreme loading, and develops CFD tools used in naval virtual design environments. MHL itself emphasizes instrumentation and DAQ for towing-tank and wind-wave experiments.

martins-joaquinn-r-r-a.summary: Joaquim Martins (Aerospace, joint NAME) heads the Multidisciplinary Design Optimization Laboratory, developing MDO techniques and applying them to aircraft and other engineering systems. Transfer is mainly computational design optimization rather than experimental marine lab work.

mckenney-thomas.lab: Great Lakes Maritime Initiative / ship design practice
mckenney-thomas.summary: Thomas McKenney is Associate Professor of Engineering Practice focused on maritime decarbonization, sustainability, and passenger vessel design/operation. He previously led ship design at the Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller Center for Zero Carbon Shipping and connects NAME teaching with applied zero-carbon ship technology pathways.

kartik-praful-naik.summary: Kartik Naik is an Assistant Research Scientist working on experimental renewable-energy harvesting concepts (underwater kites), co-design, and real-time control implementation on hardware. He continues research in RACELab on reconfigurable turbine arrays and ARPA-E SHARKS project management — a strong controls/DAQ/hardware bridge.

jonathan-page.lab: BRIDGE Initiative / naval systems design practice
jonathan-page.summary: Jonathan Page is Professor of Engineering Practice (NAVSEA Professor of Naval Systems Engineering). His research centers on flexibility in engineering design, real options, set-based design for maritime systems of systems, and design-tool/workforce development for naval engineering.

pan-yulin.summary: Yulin Pan leads the Flow Physics & Engineering Lab, focusing on theoretical and computational hydrodynamics with applications in ocean engineering. Topics include nonlinear ocean wave mechanics, wave turbulence, propeller and bio-inspired foil propulsion, and ship/offshore response in wave fields, with some experimental investigations of wave turbulence physics.

alan-papalia.summary: Alan Papalia directs the Robotic Exploration Lab, working on robust and certifiable algorithms for robot navigation, environmental monitoring, marine robotics, and perception in challenging environments. Strong sensing/autonomy overlap for instrumented marine platforms.

sareen-anchal.summary: Anchal Sareen leads the Experimental Fluid Dynamics Laboratory, developing flow-control strategies for unmanned underwater/aerial vehicles, bio-inspired propulsion, and renewable-energy harvesting. Research interests include experimental hydrodynamics, fluid-structure interaction, and smart morphable surfaces — a high-value experimental instrumentation target.

singer-david-j.summary: David Singer directs the Advanced Naval Concepts Research Lab and NAVSEA Ship Production Science Program. Research covers ship design theory, set-based design, ship arrangements, complexity/network science for naval combatants, and design decision frameworks used in Navy rapid ship design environments.

sun-jing.summary: Jing Sun leads RACELab, applying control theory and optimization to marine and automotive propulsion systems. Work includes modeling/identification, control algorithm development, rapid prototyping, and experimental validation for marine surface vessels, fuel-cell/turbocharger systems, and electrified energy management — a direct controls/DAQ bridge.

vlahopoulos-nickolas.summary: Nickolas Vlahopoulos (Graduate Program Chair) works on computational structural acoustics, multi-discipline ship design under uncertainty, and blast/shock simulations. Expertise includes FEM/BEM, energy finite element analysis, and optimization algorithms for complex naval systems.

methods: numerical modeling of waves and turbulence
wu-yue-cynthia.summary: Yue (Cynthia) Wu is an Assistant Research Scientist studying dynamics and energetics of waves and turbulence in the ocean and atmosphere. She uses theoretical and numerical approaches for geostrophic turbulence, gravity/lee/acoustic waves, and wave-turbulence interactions — more theory/computation than wet-lab instrumentation.

zuo-lei.summary: Lei Zuo works on marine renewable energy (ocean waves, tidal currents, offshore wind), blue economy, energy harvesting, vibration/dynamics and control, and mechatronics design. His group builds electromechanical energy-harvesting and control systems with strong experimental hardware character.

mccoy-timothy.summary: Timothy McCoy (Adjunct / Engineering Practice) established the Marine Engineering Laboratory with ONR funding — a multi-physics hardware lab with scaled shipboard electric power/propulsion, seawater cooling, and fuel systems. MEL uses a data acquisition and control system managing over 100 signals to study machinery reliability and enable autonomous machinery for surface vessels. Strong experimental DAQ/controls bridge despite adjunct title.

zhigang-wei.lab: Computational mechanics / ship hydrodynamics research support
zhigang-wei.summary: Zhigang Wei is an Associate Research Scientist on the NAME research-faculty track. Public profile details are sparse; deep-research sources describe support for computational mechanics and ship hydrodynamics / CFD modeling within the department. Verify current project focus on the profile or with the PI before outreach.
